title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data handling failure in a developer tool, not a model error. The upload happened at the client, on the developer's own machine, through a feature that shipped enabled by default. Nothing in the reporting describes a model asserting anything false or a system used outside its intended conditions. The failure is that the default configuration of a locally installed assistant sent local repositories to a remote cloud service, and the user was not asked.

Catching this would have required a consent step before any repository left the machine, or a default of off for the indexing feature with an explicit opt in. It would also have required review of what the shipped defaults actually did, and monitoring of outbound traffic from the tool. The behaviour was reported by developers rather than surfaced by the vendor, which places the detection outside the deployment.

What is not established is intent. The retracted claim about six workspaces containing sensitive data is not a finding, and Z.ai's statement that independent reviews found no code data retained is the company's own account rather than an outside determination.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Developers reported that Z.ai's ZCode AI coding assistant uploaded local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without consent. Z.ai said a default-enabled Codebase Indexing feature caused the behavior. It apologized, patched the vulnerability, and later disabled the upload path. One company retracted a separate claim that six workspaces containing sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai said independent reviews found no code data retained.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
